title: Large language models in medicine
explain_beginner: Large language models, the AI systems behind tools like ChatGPT, are being rapidly adopted in medicine. They show promise in tasks ranging from helping doctors pass licensing exams to automatically summarizing patient records. This survey examines how these models are entering healthcare and what they can do. Understanding these capabilities matters because they could transform how doctors work and improve patient care, but we need reliable information about what they can and cannot do.
explain_business: Large language models are moving into healthcare applications with measurable technical capabilities demonstrated across multiple domains. Organizations considering adoption should recognize that viable use cases exist, from clinical decision support to documentation management. However, the landscape is still rapidly evolving with diverse model types showing different strengths. Decision-makers should treat this as an emerging opportunity requiring careful evaluation of specific applications rather than broad implementation, informed by documented performance on relevant medical tasks.
explain_practitioner: This primer reviews the emerging applications of large language models in clinical practice and medical research. The scope includes systems demonstrating performance on standardized medical assessments and document processing applications. The authors, publishing through KOSMI's special issue, synthesize current developments in LLM deployment across healthcare domains. The key finding is that multiple specialized implementations exist, each with distinct capabilities, requiring practitioners to understand specific use cases and performance characteristics when evaluating integration into clinical workflows.
